videos.title_guess: The Closing Room (Nov 10, 2026) – Top Producer John Stevenson on Trust, Capping the Company, and Video-Based Selling
videos.summary: Weekly Closing Room training call hosted by COO Bruce Jensen featuring John Stevenson, described as Annuity.com's #1 producer who works with no staff, relying on systems. John explains how the annuity.com brand, agent 'ownership' (stock earned by production) and search visibility transfer trust to him when clients vet him online. Bruce explains the 'Cap the Company' program and John describes capping in 6 months, then 3 months, then ~5 weeks, and reinvesting overrides into marketing. John then screen-shares Annuity Genius to show how he answers MYGA inquiries with personalized screen-recorded videos that compare MYGAs, ratings and income riders transparently. He ends with a contrarian follow-up philosophy: provide heavy value up front, act unneedy, and never chase.

terms_definitions.definition: Producing more than $5 million and more than $50,000 in overrides ('company dollars') in an anniversary year; after that point the agent receives all the overrides on further business. Resets each anniversary year.
The carrier-published commission paid to the agent; e.g., 7% on a $100,000 indexed annuity income rider = $7,000.
Extra commission carriers pay the IMO on top of street commission; John estimates 1.5%–2.5%, averaging ~2%, lower for MYGAs and SPIAs; Annuity.com passes it back to capped agents.
John: 'basically buying a CD' – fixed-rate, principal-protected; provides income only for a term then renews at the then-current rate; not lifetime income.
A rider (with a rider charge) that grows a benefit base (e.g., 10% simple roll-up) on which lifetime withdrawal % is applied; account value and death benefit may be depleted but income is guaranteed.
Bruce: the core challenge in sales is how fast trust transfers to you; brand association, in-person meetings, source of lead/referral, and education all transfer trust.
Rates sometimes seen online that agents can't find are advisory products sold by registered advisors who charge an annual fee that erodes total yield, often below commission-based products.
John: B++ companies have fewer reserves than A- or A; he prefers B++ or higher, and splits large deposits (e.g., $1M) or favors A+ for big premiums; state guaranty coverage matters to some clients.

claims_stats.claim: COMPANY: Producing roughly $1 million a year earns 'a piece of ownership' (stock) at Annuity.com (Bruce: 'Just a million').
COMPANY: Cap the Company = >$5M production AND >$50K overrides in an anniversary year; all overrides afterward go to the agent.
COMPANY/ANECDOTE: John took 6 months to cap in year 1, 3 months in year 2, and ~30 days/5–5.5 weeks in year 3.
COMPANY: Typical overrides cited: 1.5%, 2%, or 2.5% by carrier, ~2% average; less for MYGAs and SPIAs.
EXAMPLE: $100,000 sold at 7% = $7,000 street commission; expect ~$2,000–$2,500 override if capped.
EXAMPLE: $1M/month production ≈ $70K commission + ~$20K overrides, which John would reinvest in marketing (seminars, mailers).
ANECDOTE: John lost a $1M rollover client because she couldn't find him online – ~$70K commission lost.
John's book cost about $25,000 to produce; he says brand matters more than the book; uses book as a post-sale gift.
COMPANY: LeadPro subscribers now get free leads out of the Financialize relationship; Annuity.com has invested in organic search so unpaid inbound leads arrive.
EXAMPLE (Annuity Genius, caption-noisy): $800K, 5-year MYGA top rate around 6.15–6.3%, grows to ~$1.078M after 5 years; a top rated carrier allowed 10% free withdrawal after year 1.

EXAMPLE: Global Atlantic income rider on $800K: benefit base grows to ~$1.2M with 10% simple roll-up; at ~8.02% withdrawal ≈ $96K/year for life vs ~$86K/yr from annuitizing the $1.078M MYGA at 8%. [Numbers partly unclear in caption.]
Commissions John has seen: MYGAs as low as ~0.5%–1.5%; income riders ~7% + ~2.5% override.
John says he does not follow up with prospects anymore; a very small number (1–2) of sales close without a meeting; most still meet by Zoom after multiple video replies.
An applicant John 'pushed away' ('maybe you shouldn't buy an annuity') ended up submitting two applications.

sales_teachings.detail: Clients Google your name + 'annuities'; showing up as Annuity.com agent plus saying 'I'm an owner' creates instant credibility for large rollovers. Fill out your agents.annuity.com profile (intro YouTube video, Google local info, AI-assisted copy) so you appear in Google/AI search.
'Biggest way to gain trust is educating'; teaching makes the client's brain associate you with expertise and prompts follow-up questions.

Use Screencast/Loom with your face in the corner; show the client's requested product plus alternatives (top 5-year MYGAs, withdrawal features, ratings, income rider comparison). 2–5 minute videos; answer an emailed question list item by item; keep emails as a compliance trail; spouse can watch too.

Show multiple carriers and tradeoffs, disclose that you could earn more selling other products; never push the high-commission product. Bruce: John never looks at commission; he sells 0.5% MYGAs and 7%+ riders based on need.
Ask questions first to discover the need; product presentation just confirms the need ('confirmation bias, not sales bias').

Ask: Are you looking for MYGA (CD-like)? Fixed rate? Do you want lifetime income? MYGA gives term income then renews; if lifetime income is the sole goal, show the income rider instead; MYGA only if flexibility is wanted.
Ask for rating preference; explain B++ vs A-/A+ tradeoff (slightly lower rating often = more income); state personal preference and cut up large premiums across carriers.

Send everything up front; close the email with 'let me know if you have questions… if you decide to lock in the rate by submitting an application, I'd love to help'; then never call again. Act confident, not needy; pushing away can increase pull.
Don't throw other advisors under the bus; say limited carriers are easier to run a practice with but not usually in client's best interest.

notable_quotes.quote: it's all about the transfer of trust. And the faster you can get the transfer of trust to you the more effective that you can be.
the biggest way that you can gain people's trust is by educating
I try to provide so much value up front and then I try to act like I don't care.
pushing people away makes them want to work with you more.
You're simply saying, okay, I heard you say this. Let me show you... It becomes a confirmation bias that you create with the client instead of a sales bias.
people appreciate the transparency.
they're going to do their research online.
You don't need to sit there and tell them what they need to do. Just explore it with them, educate them.

videos.summary: Monthly third-Tuesday Annuity.com community call that recognizes August 2025 top achievers, shareholder-club/pinnacle producers, and agency builders, then turns to CEO Brett Blake's company update. Brett reports growth from ~300 agents in June to 491 at end of August, outlines a strategic shift toward recruiting brand-new, life-only and Medicare agents supported by team selling and AI tools, and gives share valuation of $6–$9 vs $1 a year earlier. He previews the 'Race to a Million' stock incentive for agency builders (launch target Oct 1), the Senior Annuity Agent program with a commission-split lead test, and a proof-of-concept multi-agent annuity AI. He closes with a vision of $50–100 billion in annual annuity production at ~5% of a $2.3 trillion market.

videos.title_guess: The Closing Room with Tom Hegna – Handling Objections (fall 2025, ~Oct/Nov)
videos.summary: Tom Hegna, long-time annuity educator, joins the Closing Room (despite a cold and travel fatigue) to teach objection handling: thank, empathize, ask 'may I ask why?', show value, use disinterested third-party research. He rebuts common objections (fees, commissions, liquidity, taxes, FDIC, market upside, inflation, 100% stocks) with analogies and data. He explains why fall is 'CD season', promotes MYGA as CD competitor with 'triple interest', and teaches the Social Security tax torpedo conversation as a no-selling lead generator. Brett Blake and Bruce Jensen add market-size data, the Wade Pfau RISA segmentation, and Wealth Logics software for sequence-of-returns and LTC illustrations.

Poor market returns in the first years of withdrawals can exhaust a portfolio even if average returns are high.
Staying 100% in stocks may work in accumulation but not once taking income (distribution).
Contrasted with FIA as the right comparison for market-participation clients (named alongside variable annuity).

videos.title_guess: Medicare Agents Selling Annuities – the RAMP Program (Brett Blake)
videos.summary: Brett Blake introduces RAMP (Reducing Annual Medicare Penalties), an Annuity.com program that helps Medicare agents add annuities by calling current clients with a 3-minute IRMAA checker and a Social Security tax torpedo check. Online tools qualify clients and the agent then hands off to a specialist via team selling, so agents only need to set the appointment. Compensation is 100% street commission with an agreed split (up to 20% to the senior advisor), plus stock options, agency builder program and production bonuses. Licensing needs are a life license plus 4–8 hours one-time suitability training, with LeadPro as an optional paid tool and free joining.

synthesis:
BATCH 1 SYNTHESIS (5 videos). COMPANY FACTS (Annuity.com) vs EDUCATIONAL CONTENT are tagged in claims. 
COMPANY POSITIONING: Annuity.com = agent-first IMO (≈17–18 months old in late 2025; led by CEO Brett Blake since Jan 2024; COO Bruce Jensen; CTO Alan Culver; back office ECA Marketing). Core promises: free to join; 100% street commission, no IMO fee; Cap the Company (>$5M production and >$50K overrides in an anniversary year => keep all overrides; John Stevenson capped in 6 mo, 3 mo, ~5 wks); stock ownership (≈$1M production earns a sliver; tiers: Shareholders Club $1M, Equity Alliance $3M, Pinnacle $5M = $15K shares); Agency Builder program (7 degrees, 50% of earnings shared; Race to a Million stock incentive planned Oct 1 2025); 'compensation plan not commission plan'; written no-captivity promise. Scale: 300 agents (Jun 2025) → 491 (Aug) → 600 (Nov 5); 60+ carriers, 2,400+ products; share valuation $6–9 vs $1 a year earlier (company-reported, not independently verified). Growth strategy: recruit brand-new, life-only and Medicare agents via team selling (new agent sets appointment; Senior Annuity Agent handles case design/presentation/funding), WIN ('what is your number', 'two wins a day') and RAMP/IRMAA + SS tax-torpedo checkers; performance pathways (qualified lead, seminar, team selling). Products/tools: LeadPro (CRM + website + newsletters + directory listing; $299 setup and a monthly fee—captions say '$1.99/mo' in two videos, almost certainly $199/mo [unclear]), Tom Hegna On Demand ($97/mo value, free to LeadPro subscribers from Jan 1 2026), Agent Assist AI GPT (don't enter client names; proprietary multi-agent AI 'Agent IQ' targeted 2026), Annuity.com Find-an-Agent directory, agents.annuity.com profile/AI-search visibility, Financialize-vetted free leads for LeadPro subscribers/senior agents. 
CROSS-VIDEO THEMES: (1) Trust transfer is the central sales variable—brand (annuity.com as 'industry URL'), ownership claim, online searchability, education, third-party research (Hegna), and personalized video (Stevenson). Brett (Nov 5) and John both report brand raises completion of rollovers/transfers; John lost a $1M rollover to being unfindable. (2) Needs-based, non-pushy selling: 'stop selling—find and solve problems' (Hegna), 'match the need, confirmation not sales bias' (Bruce), rate/carrier agnosticism and commission transparency (Stevenson), 'I'm not the specialist' (RAMP). (3) Entry hooks that avoid selling: WIN number, IRMAA 3-minute check, SS tax torpedo, CD-season MYGA talk. Tax torpedo appears in both Hegna and RAMP—Hegna's thresholds ($34K single/$44K married, unindexed since 1994) are the educational anchor. (4) Industry sizing repeated consistently: ~10–11K retirees/day, 98% growth 2020–2024 ($219B→$434B), 54% would buy vs ≤12% own, $2.3T opportunity (Boston College CRR), $32T–$90T transfers/rollovers; Hegna/Brett speak of ~$465B vs $2.3T demand. Treat figures as speaker-stated. (5) Compensation education: typical commissions 1% (MYGA) to ~8% (FIA); $100K at 7% = $7,000; override ~1.5–2.5%; 10% total split 3% company/7% agent (illustration).
EDUCATIONAL CONTENT HIGHLIGHTS (Hegna): objection framework (thank, empathize, 'may I ask why?', value, third-party proof); most annuities are spread products with no fees (only VAs and riders); commission paid by insurer not client vs advisory fee from account; liquidity = lifetime event; 'triple interest' for MYGA; sequence-of-returns, never withdraw from a falling account; RISA segmentation 35/35–40/25; ladder annuities vs inflation; AI/software side-by-side beats advisors in decumulation. Stevenson: MYGA vs income-rider comparison (e.g. $800K → $1.078M MYGA vs ~$1.2M benefit base at ~8% ≈ $96K/yr) and ratings preference (B++ or higher; split large premiums).
CAVEATS FOR DOWNSTREAM USE: Several figures are caption-garbled (YTD production '165 million', LeadPro price, '$6,800 a month' torpedo example, Equity Alliance award numbers, name spellings Broach/Brooch, Carillo/Krill, Snar, Dibwad). Hegna's 'most annuities have no fees' and SS thresholds are speaker claims—verify against carrier/IRS sources before publishing in SEO/GEO content (SS combined-income tiers actually include a 50% tier; Hegna cites only 85% thresholds). Compliance: avoid income-guarantee implications; RAMP script must be used outside Medicare enrollment appointments per CMS rules. Date oddity: file title says Nov 10 2026 for the Stevenson Closing Room, other files are Sep/Nov 2025; confirm date.
